title: Ops SLO field lab journal and quick experiments
summary: Working journal for small rapid experiments and cross-team decisions to shape the SLO rollout. Less polished than playbooks; intended to record what we tried, why, and quick outcomes.
notes:
Context:
- Objective: trial multiple measurement and rollback techniques in a controlled field lab before final SLO adoption across hosted/dedicated surfaces.
- Audience: eng-sre + eng-platform + product-hosted-api + release-eng. Keep notes minimal and actionable.

Quick experiment log (entries newest first):
- 2026-03-09 | Experiment: low-cardinality trace aggregation prototype
  - What: ingest traces with model+region tags only for >72h then emit aggregated span counts nightly.
  - Why: reduce storage while preserving incident attribution signal.
  - Who: Nina (lead), infra prototype script.
  - Result: query latency for aggregated traces acceptable; edge-case for rare models lost. Action: keep, but mark low-traffic models for 7d retention.

- 2026-03-07 | Experiment: cache-aware latency measurement
  - What: produce two latency series: raw_request_latency and warm_cache_latency_excluded.
  - Why: customers see different experience when prefix/KV cache hits are common; team wants to know both.
  - Who: Owen ran synthetic test load.
  - Result: p99 diverged by ~30ms on high cache-hit flows. Decision: measure both and use warm-cache-excluded for alerting; flag raw for product dashboards.

- 2026-03-06 | Experiment: micro-canary rollback speed test
  - What: simulate automatic rollback on error budget breach and measure time to re-route traffic.
  - Who: Hannah configured routing shim.
  - Result: median rollback 14s, 95th 48s due to DNS propagation on one cluster. Action: add health-check based immediate routing step to avoid DNS waits.

Minimal launch checklist (short actionable items):
- Metrics emitted: p50/p95/p99 histograms; request_success boolean; route and model tags mandatory. Owner: eng-serving-runtime. ETA: 2026-03-12.
- Alert policy draft: soft page at 1.5x error budget burn in 7d; hard page at sustained 3h breach. Owner: eng-sre. ETA: 2026-03-14.
- Canary pipeline: 1% -> 10% -> 40% -> 100%. Auto-rollback trigger: sustained p99 > baseline * 1.25 for 30m. Owner: eng-platform. ETA: 2026-03-20.
- Runbooks: one-page playbook + one-click incident kickstarter. Owner: release-eng. ETA: 2026-03-18.

Cross-team decision notes (short):
- Tag enforcement: ingestion will reject metrics missing product/model tags. Temporary shim accepted. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Retention policy: full traces 7d for top-10 models, 72h for others, then aggregated. Owner: eng-infra. Decision in favor with caveat to revisit after month.
- SLO split: embeddings get a separate SLO and throttle policy; not included in main text-gen SLO. Product agreed.

Risks observed during field tests:
- Noisy low-traffic services produce alerts. Mitigation: add minimum sample volume gating to alert rules.
- Attribution gaps when requests cross shared routing layer. Mitigation: propagate X-RW-ORIGIN header and stitch using trace id.

Open questions to resolve before formal playbook: (ranked)
1) Minimum sample threshold for paging low-volume models? (in progress)
2) Exact error budget math for multi-tenant incidents (how to split burn).
3) SLA vs SLO communication template for CS.

Next quick wins (each ~1-3 days):
- Implement sample-volume gating in alert tests (Owen).
- Add short customer-facing blurb template for CS (Hannah).
- Finalize retention tiers and start cost projection (Nina + eng-infra).

Meeting cadence proposal (lightweight):
- Twice-weekly 30m field-lab sync for next 6 weeks (owner Marcus).
- Ad-hoc tabletop day the week before canary start.

Reference snippets for the playbook (copy-paste ready):
- Canary rollback procedure: Step 1: route off canary (health-check circuit). Step 2: evaluate error budget signal. Step 3: notify SRE rotation + product lead. Step 4: escalate to oncall pager if unable to return to baseline in 30m.
- Alert gating: require >= 1000 requests in 24h window for model-level paging; otherwise create ticket but do not page.

Appendix: owners and quick contacts
- eng-sre lead: Marcus Liu (marcus@redwood.ai)
- eng-platform: Owen Reed (owen@redwood.ai)
- release-engineering: Hannah Park (hannah@redwood.ai)
- infra prototype: Nina Patel (nina@redwood.ai)

Decision log (bullet list):
- 2026-03-07: Adopt separate warm-cache-excluded series for primary SLO (Marcus).
- 2026-03-09: Approve aggregated traces after 72h for non-top10 models (team consensus).
- 2026-03-06: Add health-check immediate routing to rollback steps to avoid DNS delay (Hannah).

End of journal entry. Keep this doc as the ephemeral record of field trials; transfer consolidated decisions to the canonical SLO playbook once stable.
